title: EXTRACTORS key mismatch breaks incremental extraction
description: EXTRACTORS constant uses plural keys (:models, :controllers) but re_extract_unit looks up by singular type (:model, :controller). Incremental extraction silently fails to find the correct extractor for any unit.

title: Missing types in re_extract_unit
description: The case statement in re_extract_unit only handles :model, :controller, :service, :component. Missing: :job, :mailer, :graphql_type, :graphql_mutation, :graphql_resolver, :graphql_query, :rails_source.

title: API controllers silently omitted from extraction
description: Controller discovery uses ApplicationController.descendants, which misses controllers inheriting from ActionController::API. API-only controllers are invisible to extraction.

title: Config extractors default missing 4 of 8 types
description: Default extractors config only lists :models, :controllers, :services, :components. Missing: :jobs, :mailers, :graphql, :rails_source.

title: Missing app/graphql/ in incremental file patterns
description: Incremental rake task scans app/models/, app/controllers/, app/services/, app/components/ but not app/graphql/. GraphQL type changes are never detected.

title: Missing eager_load! in incremental path
description: Full extraction calls eager_load! but incremental path may skip it, meaning newly-added classes won't be found.

title: Token estimation underestimates Ruby code by 15-25%
description: The (length / 4.0).ceil heuristic underestimates tokens for Ruby code. Ruby syntax (symbols, do/end, underscored_names) produces more tokens per character than natural language.

title: ViewComponent metadata uses Phlex-specific patterns
description: Phlex extractor metadata structure is Phlex-specific. A future ViewComponent extractor needs different metadata patterns.

title: Score fusion in hybrid search is ad-hoc, needs RRF
description: merge_candidates uses ad-hoc weighted score fusion. Should use Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF): score(d) = sum(1/(k + rank_i(d))) where k=60.

title: SQL injection pattern in Pgvector adapter pseudocode
description: Pgvector build_where interpolates filter values directly into SQL. Should use parameterized queries.

title: No cross-encoder reranking stage in retrieval pipeline
description: Pipeline goes from initial ranking to context assembly with no reranking. Cross-encoder reranking would improve precision for code search.

title: Missing chunking for scopes and per-concern source
description: Scopes and per-concern chunks are specified in chunking strategy but not yet implemented in extraction.

title: Embedding pipeline has no resumability
description: No checkpoint mechanism for embedding pipeline. Mid-batch failures require starting over.

title: No agent-as-operator design (extraction management, pipeline diagnostics)
description: No design for agents running extraction, managing the embedding pipeline, or diagnosing failures. Agents can only consume, not operate.

title: No multi-agent coordination design
description: No design for multiple agents working with the same index concurrently. Missing: shared state model, locking, handoff patterns, token budget coordination.

title: No agent self-service and diagnostics design
description: No design for agents assessing retrieval quality, reporting gaps, or requesting improvements.

title: Concurrent indexing safety not documented
description: No documentation of which operations are safe for concurrent access and which require serialization.

title: Transitive invalidation not bridged between extraction and embedding
description: When extraction produces new units, the embedding layer needs notification. No design for this bridge.

title: Agent-driven operations not documented
description: No design for how agents trigger and monitor pipeline tasks (extraction, embedding, validation).

title: Fix token estimation inconsistency across docs
description: Code uses / 3.5 (CLAUDE.md). RETRIEVAL_ARCHITECTURE.md pseudocode uses / 4.0 in TokenCounter class. MODEL_EXTRACTION_FIXES.md says / 4. Should all reference 3.5.

title: Resolve remaining cross-doc contradictions from REVIEW_FINDINGS.md
description: REVIEW_FINDINGS.md CC-001 through CC-011 identified contradictions. Many resolved, some remain (tool count mismatch PROPOSAL vs AGENTIC_STRATEGY, default vector store, default embedding provider). Systematic pass needed.

title: Update stale plan doc status line
description: Says 'Status: Design approved, ready for implementation planning' but AST/RubyAnalyzer/Flow are all complete. Update to reflect implemented state.

title: Add gem-level specs for service_extractor
description: ServiceExtractor has no gem-level unit specs. Needs tests for: happy path extraction, edge cases (empty files, namespaced classes), dependency detection.

title: Add gem-level specs for job_extractor
description: JobExtractor has no gem-level unit specs. Needs tests for: happy path extraction, edge cases (empty files, namespaced classes), dependency detection.

title: Add gem-level specs for mailer_extractor
description: MailerExtractor has no gem-level unit specs. Needs tests for: happy path extraction, edge cases (empty files, namespaced classes), dependency detection.

title: Add gem-level specs for graphql_extractor
description: GraphqlExtractor has no gem-level unit specs. Needs tests for: happy path extraction, edge cases (empty files, namespaced classes), dependency detection.

title: Add gem-level specs for rails_source_extractor
description: RailsSourceExtractor has no gem-level unit specs. Needs tests for: happy path extraction, importance rating, public API detection.

title: Implement VectorStore interface and in-memory adapter
description: Define interface: #store, #search, #delete, #count. In-memory adapter uses hash + cosine similarity. Zero-dependency baseline.

title: Implement MetadataStore interface and SQLite adapter
description: Unit metadata, type indexes, file paths, git data. SQLite for zero-dependency local usage.

title: Implement GraphStore interface wrapping DependencyGraph
description: Existing DependencyGraph is the in-memory implementation. Wrap behind interface for future PG/MySQL backends.

title: Implement EmbeddingProvider interface and Ollama adapter
description: Interface: #embed(text), #embed_batch(texts), #dimensions. Ollama first (zero external API cost), OpenAI second.

title: Implement text preparation pipeline
description: Per CONTEXT_AND_CHUNKING.md: chunk selection, prefix formatting, token limit enforcement.

title: Implement indexing pipeline orchestrator
description: Reads ExtractedUnit JSON → prepares text → embeds → stores. Full + incremental modes via content_hash. Rake tasks: woods:embed, woods:embed_incremental. Includes checkpoint/resumability for mid-batch failures. Depends on: B-028, B-031, B-032.

title: Implement query classifier
description: Classify by intent (lookup, trace, explain, compare), scope (specific, bounded, broad), depth. Heuristic-based.

title: Implement search executor with strategy selection
description: Maps classification → strategy (vector, keyword, graph, hybrid, direct). Executes against storage backends. Depends on: B-028, B-029, B-030, B-034.

title: Implement ranker with RRF
description: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60) for combining multi-strategy results. Incorporates recency, PageRank, type-match signals. Depends on: B-035.

title: Implement context assembler
description: Token-budgeted assembly: 10% structural, 50% primary, 25% supporting, 15% framework. Source attribution. Depends on: B-036.

title: Retriever orchestrator
description: Top-level Retriever class wiring classify → search → rank → assemble → format pipeline. Includes RetrievalResult struct and StructuralContextBuilder for 10% structural token budget.

title: StructuralContextBuilder (part of Retriever)
description: Private helper in Retriever that queries metadata_store for unit counts by type, generating codebase overview for the structural context budget.

title: Context formatting base + ClaudeAdapter
description: Abstract Formatting::Base with #format interface and #estimate_tokens helper. ClaudeAdapter outputs XML tags (<codebase-context>, <unit>, <source>) for Claude API/MCP.

title: GPTAdapter + GenericAdapter + HumanAdapter
description: GPTAdapter (Markdown headers + fenced code), GenericAdapter (plain text with separators), HumanAdapter (box-drawing chars for terminal).

title: Pgvector vector store adapter
description: VectorStore::Pgvector for PostgreSQL teams. HNSW index, parameterized SQL, cosine distance, filter translation to WHERE clauses, ensure_schema! for auto-setup.

title: Qdrant vector store adapter
description: VectorStore::Qdrant via HTTP REST API. Qdrant-format filter translation, collection auto-creation, no gem dependencies.

title: Instrumentation module
description: Thin wrapper around ActiveSupport::Notifications with fallback to direct yield when AS unavailable (MCP server without Rails).

title: StructuredLogger
description: JSON-line logger for pipeline operations. Supports info/warn/error/debug levels with timestamps and structured data.

title: HealthCheck
description: Reports system component status (:ok, :error, :not_configured) for vector_store, metadata_store, embedding_provider.

title: CircuitBreaker
description: Three-state pattern (closed → open → half_open) protecting external service calls. Configurable threshold and reset_timeout. Raises CircuitOpenError when open.

title: RetryableProvider
description: Decorator wrapping Embedding::Provider::Interface with exponential backoff and circuit breaker integration. Never retries CircuitOpenError.

title: IndexValidator
description: Validates extraction output health: _index.json existence, file references, content hash integrity, stale file detection. Returns ValidationReport.

title: OpenAI embedding adapter
description: Provider::OpenAI supporting text-embedding-3-small (1536d) and text-embedding-3-large (3072d). HTTPS with Bearer auth, batch embedding with index-preservation.

title: MCP codebase_retrieve tool
description: Semantic search tool added to MCP server. Accepts query + optional budget, returns formatted context + source attributions. Graceful degradation when no retriever configured.

title: Retrieval + embedding rake tasks
description: Three rake tasks: woods:retrieve[query] (CLI retrieval with HumanAdapter), woods:embed (full embedding pipeline), woods:embed_incremental (content_hash-based).

title: Wire console_eval behind WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL + EvalGuard (v0.2)
description: Embedded-mode console_eval is hard-refused at dispatch (EmbeddedExecutor#refusal_for), so EvalGuard is unreachable on the shipped path. The refusal message already advertises WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL + a Rails.env.production? rejection as the opt-in contract, but the execution wiring is not implemented. Deliver the full contract before running any Ruby: (1) gate on both config.console_unsafe_eval_enabled AND ENV['WOODS_CONSOLE_UNSAFE_EVAL']; (2) refuse unconditionally when Rails.env.production?; (3) run EvalGuard.check! before dispatch; (4) require Confirmation approval; (5) record the run in AuditLogger. Partial wiring is worse than the current refusal — ship all five or none. Tracked in issue #87 (option 2 deferral). RESOLVED: EmbeddedExecutor#handle_eval now runs all five controls (guard → confirmation → SafeContext → Timeout → audit). Server.build_embedded fails closed at boot when the flag is on but a Confirmation or audit-log path is missing.

title: Extract BridgeProtocol constants module from StubBridge
description: Issue #82 renamed Woods::Console::Bridge to StubBridge so the scaffold status is obvious. The downstream smell — flagged by both reviewers — is that the canonical protocol contract (SUPPORTED_TOOLS, TIER1_TOOLS, TOOL_HANDLERS) still lives on the stub class. EmbeddedExecutor::TIER1_TOOLS = StubBridge::TIER1_TOOLS reads as 'the real executor borrows constants from the stub', which is backwards. Extract a Woods::Console::BridgeProtocol module owning the three constants; have StubBridge include or reference it; update EmbeddedExecutor to read from BridgeProtocol directly. When the real bridge-process implementation lands it can claim the Bridge class name without the protocol contract migrating with it. Pre-existing doc-rot in docs/design/CONSOLE_SERVER.md (sections 107/118/130 still describe rails runner lib/woods/console/bridge.rb as if it works) is in scope for the same PR. RESOLVED: new lib/woods/console/bridge_protocol.rb owns SUPPORTED_TOOLS / TIER1_TOOLS / TOOL_HANDLERS. StubBridge references BridgeProtocol (top-level aliases keep StubBridge::SUPPORTED_TOOLS working for existing callers). EmbeddedExecutor reads TIER1_TOOLS = BridgeProtocol::TIER1_TOOLS and no longer imports bridge.rb. CONSOLE_SERVER.md Connection Modes section carries a callout that the three rails-runner configs describe the target bridge-process architecture, not the shipping state.

title: Wire extraction-side writes when the first durable GraphStore adapter lands
description: The boot-time hydration path (Bootstrapper.hydrated_graph_store) now raises Woods::Storage::InapplicableBackend when the configured graph_store reports durable? => true, mirroring the Snapshotter::Vector pattern for pgvector/Qdrant. This is a tripwire, not a solution: it loudly refuses to rebuild a durable store from dependency_graph.json at boot, but leaves the durable store empty because nothing populates it. When the first durable GraphStore adapter lands (:mysql, :pgvector_graph, Neo4j, etc.), that PR must also wire an extraction-side write path: graph edges are produced by Extractor, not Indexer, so the write hook belongs at the same seam that writes dependency_graph.json (see Extractor#extract_all around output_dir.join('dependency_graph.json')). The contract being honored is documented in lib/woods/storage/graph_store.rb Interface#durable? YARD, Bootstrapper.hydrated_graph_store YARD, and docs/design/PERSISTENCE_AND_BOOTSTRAP.md §3.5. Do NOT design a speculative write API before the concrete adapter exists — bulk-load semantics differ too much across backends (Postgres COPY vs MySQL batched INSERT vs Neo4j UNWIND+MERGE) and a speculative API will get rewritten.

title: Obsidian vault exporter (human graph-view + agent sidecar)
description: Export extraction artifacts to a self-contained Obsidian vault (folder of interlinked Markdown notes) so a human can explore the app in Obsidian's graph view + Bases, and an agent can load the whole topology from a _woods/ sidecar in one read. One note per unit; wikilinks encode dependencies; flat YAML frontmatter (nested props are unsupported by Obsidian Properties, so structured edges live in the sidecar + body). Reads the flat extraction output via IndexReader using raw_graph_data (string keys, persisted pagerank); all edges derive from a single in-memory edge_map (graph edges/reverse), per-unit JSON used only for note bodies. Bare-identifier keys throughout (the graph already merges cross-type id collisions upstream). Four passes: link map -> notes -> sidecar/MOC/.obsidian-config/Units.base -> guarded stale-sweep. Sweep and .obsidian writes are both gated behind a .woods-vault ownership sentinel + a 30% purge guard mirroring Unblocked. Zero new Configuration accessors (vault_path/include_source/include_framework/force_purge are constructor kwargs, exposed via WOODS_OBSIDIAN_* env in the rake task). include_framework covers rails_source only (gem_source is unreachable via IndexReader::TYPE_DIRS). Grounded in Steph Ango / kepano vault conventions + official Obsidian docs. Shipped in #143. RESOLVED: added lib/woods/atomic_file.rb + lib/woods/obsidian/{vault_exporter,note_builder,name_mapper,vault_assets,errors}.rb + the woods:obsidian/woods:vault rake task; 49 unit specs plus an end-to-end booted-app validation (spec/integration/booted_extraction_spec.rb) that exports a real spec/dummy extraction and asserts resolvable wikilinks, no dangling links, a bijective sidecar manifest, and byte-identical re-export; docs in docs/OBSIDIAN_INTEGRATION.md + README + CLAUDE.md.

title: Extract shared UnitFacts; migrate DocumentBuilder + NoteBuilder onto it
description: Woods::Obsidian::NoteBuilder (B-056) and Woods::Unblocked::DocumentBuilder independently walk unit metadata (associations-by-type, blast-radius buckets, entry points, side effects, schema highlights, deps/dependents-by-type). That selection/shaping logic is format-agnostic; only the final string assembly (plain-text + GitHub URIs vs wikilinks + frontmatter) diverges. Extract a Woods::Export::UnitFacts that turns a unit_data hash into a structured intermediate, and make both builders thin formatters over it, so a unit-type metadata change is fixed in one place. PREREQUISITE: Unblocked detects changes by hashing the rendered body (Exporter#fingerprint = SHA256(title + body)), and its specs guard determinism/structure but NOT byte-exact output, so a refactor could pass CI green yet force a one-time mass re-push. Before touching DocumentBuilder, add golden-output regression specs that pin its exact body bytes per unit type. Until this lands, B-056 mitigates drift with a shared metadata-shape fixture asserted by both spec suites. Tracked in #144. RESOLVED: added lib/woods/export/unit_facts.rb (associations_by_type, schema_highlights, blast_radius) + specs; added spec/unblocked/document_builder_golden_spec.rb pinning DocumentBuilder body bytes per unit type against spec/fixtures/unblocked/golden_units.rb + golden/*.md; migrated DocumentBuilder model_associations + model_schema_highlights onto UnitFacts with the golden suite confirming byte-identical output (no Unblocked re-push); migrated NoteBuilder associations onto UnitFacts and added a shared Schema section; GoldenUnits is now asserted by both the Unblocked golden suite and the Obsidian NoteBuilder suite as the shared metadata-shape fixture.

title: Qdrant adapter sends Woods identifiers as point IDs — every upsert 400s
description: Qdrant only accepts uint/UUID point IDs but the adapter passed Woods identifiers ("User", "User#chunk_0") straight through, so every upsert 400s and the Qdrant path was non-functional. Fixed: point ids are now UUIDv5 over a pinned namespace (Qdrant::POINT_ID_NAMESPACE), the identifier rides in the payload under `woods_identifier`, and search reverse-maps while delete translates through the same Qdrant.point_id so it can't compute a different id than the upsert did. Translation is confined to the adapter — pgvector and the in-memory store are untouched, and the Indexer needed no change. UUIDv5 is implemented in Woods::Util::UUID5 and unit-tested against the published DNS-namespace vectors for python.org and www.example.com. STILL UNVALIDATED AGAINST A LIVE QDRANT: that a real server accepts these upserts, that a re-embed of an unchanged unit replaces rather than duplicates, and that delete actually removes the point. All current coverage is against a mocked Net::HTTP. Tracked in GH #147.

title: Incremental embed against in-memory vector store discards vectors but advances checkpoint
description: index_incremental never persist_snapshots and process_units always advances checkpoint.json, so on :local/:shared_filesystem presets changed units embed into a throwaway store, nothing is written to dumps/, and the checkpoint skips them next run — unrecoverable without full re-embed. Fix: hydrate+persist in incremental mode, or do not advance checkpoint when unpersisted. Tracked in GH #148.

title: Notion Columns sync collapses same-named columns across models
description: Column pages are upserted by bare column name and found by title equality across the whole DB, so shared columns (id/created_at/updated_at) overwrite each other across models — the Columns DB collapses to one page per distinct name. Fix: qualify title (users.id) or filter lookup by Table relation. Tracked in GH #149.

title: Audit follow-ups: medium-severity correctness/robustness findings
description: HTTP transport concurrent-handler unsynchronized IndexReader cache + lazy pipeline mutex init; Notion/Unblocked POST retry on read-timeout duplicates; Retry-After to_f zeros HTTP-date form; CircuitBreaker half-open unlimited probes + reset on overlap; bootstrapper/reload string-keyed vector metadata vs symbol-keyed search filters. Tracked in GH #150. PARTIAL (PR #151): FIXED the pipeline-lock mutex race (eager init), Retry-After (shared Woods::RetryAfter helper, both clients), and CircuitBreaker (single half-open probe + success_threshold). REMAINING: IndexReader cache guard, POST-retry idempotency, bootstrap/reload key-form normalization.

title: Dependency graph collapses same-identifier units of different types onto one node
description: DependencyGraph keys nodes on the bare identifier, so two units of different types that share one (a Scenic view `reports` from db/views/reports_v01.sql and a factory `reports` from spec/factories/reports.rb) collapse onto a single node — last registration wins, and the loser also loses its type-index entry. Both unit JSON files are still written, so the index and the graph disagree. deduplicate_results only dedupes within a type. Surfaced by the #164 differential harness, which works around it by giving each generated artifact family its own name prefix. Fix likely means keying the graph on (type, identifier) or namespacing identifiers per type, which touches every graph consumer (MCP tools, Obsidian, retrieval).

title: Two files defining the same constant resolve differently in full vs incremental extraction
description: When two source files yield units with the same identifier, full extraction keeps the first by glob order (deduplicate_results' uniq(&:identifier)) while the incremental path keeps whichever was written last. The tree is already broken in that state (Ruby would be redefining a constant), so this is a tie-break inconsistency rather than data loss, but it means full and incremental disagree. Surfaced by the #164 differential harness.

title: Phase 1-4 of the reactive index spike: in-process extractor API, woods:watch daemon, MCP freshness contract, multi-instance operation
description: Follow-on work from #164 now that phase 0 (incremental correctness + differential harness) has landed. Phase 1: a public API to re-run a single whole-app extractor against a booted app (WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS already does this internally). Phase 2: a resident file-watching daemon (woods:watch) — placement decision, restart triggers, storm handling, degraded status. Phase 3: a generation token IndexReader checks per request, plus working-tree staleness in woods_status. Phase 4: multi-worktree operation with per-daemon idle TTL. Each phase needs measurements against the success criteria in #164. RESOLVED: all four phases landed on claude/woods-issue-164-uu6tc0 (PR #165). Phase 1 = Extractor#refresh + woods:refresh + ReloadPolicy; phase 2 = Woods::Watch daemon + woods:watch; phase 3 = Woods::Generation + IndexReader self-refresh + woods_status freshness fields; phase 4 = PipelineLock write serialization, daemon deference for hook syncs, idle TTL, six-worktree spec. Outstanding and documented in docs/WATCH_DAEMON.md rather than tracked here: large-host-app latency, bind-mount event latency, and per-daemon memory at six-worktree scale — all three need a real host app.

title: Dependency graph persists absolute file paths, so the index is not portable off the machine that built it
description: dependency_graph.json stores absolute paths (file_map keys and nodes[].file_path) while every per-unit JSON stores relative ones. Ordering, not intent: extract_all rebuilds the graph at phase 1.6 and normalize_file_paths runs at phase 4.5, so registration captures the absolute string and the later reassignment of unit.file_path never reaches the copies in @nodes/@file_map. register_and_write has the same order, so full and incremental agree — this is not an equivalence bug and the #164 harness is right not to flag it. It matters for the documented Docker deployment (extraction inside the container, Index Server on the host reading the volume mount): the graph carries /app/... paths, so affected_by, identifiers_for_path and the prune sweep match nothing host-side, and a host-run woods:incremental computes an empty blast radius silently. A moved or renamed checkout has the same effect. Fix: normalize before registration and relativize at the lookup boundary. Needs a from_h migration for absolute-keyed graphs already on disk — same shape as normalize_edges and normalize_file_map, which handle pre-#164 formats without a rebuild. Surfaced by the #164 review (finding 17); deferred from PR #165 as too large for it. Tracked in GH #166.

title: GraphQL runtime introspection can emit units no per-file pass reproduces
description: GraphQLExtractor#extract_all runs a static file pass and a runtime pass (extract_from_runtime_type). PR #165 made the file pass unconditional, fixing the divergence visible without graphql-ruby loaded (the per-file path indexed types a full run dropped). Remaining: with the gem loaded, the runtime pass can emit units the file pass cannot reach — dynamically defined types, schema-builder/DSL types, anything whose constant exists only after the schema is constructed. Those units have no source file, so no changed path dispatches to them and an incremental run cannot recreate them. Fix is probably a discoverable_classes equivalent so the incremental path reconciles the runtime set in both directions like class-based types, provided the schema type map is exact by construction; otherwise move GraphQL to WHOLE_APP_EXTRACTORS. Either way needs gem 'graphql' in the version gemfiles as a dev/test dependency plus a harness template exercising a dynamic type — which is why it was left out of #165. Tracked in GH #167.
